extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers or members of the public seeking a comprehensive encyclopedic summary of the Chris Rock–Will Smith slapping incident
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive encyclopedic article summarizing a single high-profile live-television incident: background, the incident itself, immediate and longer-term aftermath, legal and institutional responses, public reactions, and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy standards of conduct (grounds for disciplinary action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy charged Smith with "violations of the Academy's standards of conduct, including inappropriate physical contact, abusive or threatening behavior, and compromising the integrity of the Academy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board of Governors can consider these categories when deciding suspension, expulsion or other sanctions; the Academy's standards of conduct were cited as the basis for the formal review and potential disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy disciplinary procedure (investigation and sanctions process)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the incident the Academy's Board of Governors announced a formal review, invited a written response within a fifteen-day period, and would vote on whether "suspension, expulsion or other sanctions under the Academy's standards of conduct" would be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural notes on the page: a Board charge → invitation for written response within 15 days → Board vote on sanctions. The page also documents practical effects: Smith's preemptive resignation altered the legally prescribed timetable and removed suspension/expulsion as possible outcomes; the Board later imposed a ten-year ban preventing attendance at any Academy events (in person or virtually).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast censorship / federal indecency rules (muting expletives on live TV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Live television broadcasts in the United States mostly muted the incident due to federal censorship laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. broadcasters censored (muted) expletives during the live broadcast citing federal censorship/indecency rules; uncensored international footage nevertheless circulated online. The Federal Communications Commission also received complaints about the incident (the page notes the FCC received 66 complaints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace conduct standard (SAG-AFTRA statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: SAG-AFTRA issued a statement condemning Smith's behavior: "Violence or physical abuse in the workplace is never appropriate and the union condemns any such conduct."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union framed on-stage physical assault as unacceptable workplace conduct and committed to working with the Academy and broadcaster to ensure appropriate action. This represents an industry standard for professional behavior at workplace events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal prosecution/practical criteria for misdemeanor battery in Los Angeles
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple legal commentators noted prosecution was unlikely if Chris Rock declined to press charges; statements included that to be arrested on a misdemeanor it often requires either the authorities witnessing it or the victim filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites: LAPD did not file charges because Rock did not wish to file a report; former prosecutors and legal analysts explained practical constraints (victim participation, witness presence, and city attorney discretion) that make misdemeanor prosecution unlikely in such circumstances, though some experts argued the public nature could prompt consideration of charges. Different experts offered competing views on probability of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of resignation on organizational disciplinary timelines and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Smith preemptively resigned his Academy membership; the Academy said that following his resignation, "suspension or expulsion are no longer a possibility and the legally prescribed timetable no longer applies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents how resignation can change the available remedies (e.g., expulsion no longer possible) and procedural timetables in organizational discipline, and that the Board may still pursue other issues (e.g., retaining the Oscar, invitation rights) despite resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy-industry response norms and practical safety guidance after on-stage violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians and comedy clubs reacted by expressing concern about future confrontations and, in some cases, announcing increased security measures. Many comedians said they might be more careful about the topics of jokes going forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements cited: some comedians worried the incident would make performers avoid sensitive topics; clubs (e.g., Laugh Factory, Stand Up NY, Carolines on Broadway) announced increased security. This functions as an informal industry guideline balancing performer content choices and venue safety protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic / fact-checking practice toward viral claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims on social media (for example, that Rock had apologized or that he wore a cheek pad) were debunked by fact-checkers and reliable outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents the role of verification: manipulated images and false social posts were later debunked by Reuters, USA Today and other fact-checkers. Implicit guidance: verify viral claims with primary sources and credible fact-checking before reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opinion and political actor response as a metric of acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Public polls and political statements were used to measure and express societal response; e.g., a YouGov poll found 61% of Americans said Smith's actions were unacceptable, while politicians publicly discussed or took positions on the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article treats opinion polls, number of complaints to regulators, and politicians' public positions as indicators of public sentiment and factors that shape reputational and institutional consequences after a high-profile incident.
